_design_note: Opponent exposure: the ONLY change from the anchor is training.opponents. It exists because of a structural gap, not a hunch. Training solo leaves the opponents plane and the living_opponents scalar identically zero for the whole run, so the first-layer weights that read them receive zero gradient and keep their random initialisation; at tournament evaluation those inputs become non-zero for the first time and inject an untrained random projection. handcrafted_v1 had the same structural gap (its opponent-bearing entries are also zero when solo), and docs/01 section 7.19 measured that closing it moved coins_share 18.6 -> 22.0 percent (3.0 sigma, above the 0.022 threshold) and survival 3.9 -> 17.4 percent, at a cost of 68 percent on solo classic. So the handcrafted evidence points at doing this, not away from it. Trained from scratch rather than fine-tuned from the anchor's checkpoints: fine-tuning would be cheaper but needs checkpoint warm-start, which INITIAL_MODEL_KINDS deliberately does not implement, and it would break the fresh-start rule every other arm in this project follows. EXPLORATION SCHEDULE: E09, counted in environment steps rather than rounds. The pilot (runs/m4_pilot_20260827) measured why: at epsilon 1.00 a loot-crate round lasts 9.8 steps because random play kills itself at once, and 210 steps once the agent survives. Under E07's 100-round hold the buffer therefore held 982 of the 10,000 transitions min_size requires, and the first gradient step did not land until round 826 -- with epsilon already annealed to 0.11, which is precisely the cold start E07 existed to provide. E09 holds epsilon at 1.00 for 10,000 steps, exactly min_size, so the first gradient step sees a full buffer at full exploration, then anneals over 200,000 steps.

_predeclared_design_numbers.budget_curve: docs/05 section 0.18 found that on the handcrafted line, training past 2000 rounds made the competition-setting score worse, reproduced across two arms. Whether that holds for a model with three orders of magnitude more parameters is open; report classic_versus_opponents at every evaluated checkpoint rather than only at the end.
_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: training.opponents [] -> three rule_based_agent. Nothing else moves.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: The M4 anchor arm at the same budget and seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.expected_cost: docs/01 section 7.15: expect solo classic to fall substantially. Report it rather than hiding it; the submitted agent is scored with opponents.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If coins_share does not move by 0.022, opponent exposure is not the bridge to G-B and the zero-gradient argument, however sound structurally, does not cash out.
_predeclared_design_numbers.gate: Learning from scratch, judged on VALIDATION seeds only so that holdout stays unselected. All three must hold: (a) the mean loot-crate validation score over the last two evaluated checkpoints exceeds the mean over the first two by more than the 4.7 resolution; (b) the final validation score is above an untrained-CNN control, which the smoke measured at score 0.0 with wait_fraction 0.998 and distinct_cells 1.9; (c) the policy is not degenerate -- distinct_cells > 20, bomb_rate > 0.01, wait_fraction < 0.6. Point-to-point monotonicity is NOT required and must not be used: an RL curve that dips once is not a failed arm.
_predeclared_design_numbers.known_limitation: Training is solo, so the opponents plane and the living_opponents scalar are identically zero throughout and the weights reading them keep their initialisation. At tournament evaluation those inputs become non-zero for the first time. This arm therefore cannot answer whether the representation helps against opponents; the opponent-exposure arm exists for that.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: classic_versus_opponents coins_share exceeds the anchor's by more than 0.022. No prediction on official score, which docs/01 section 7.20 shows resolves worse.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Quote evaluation_summary.json reportable_result, never selected_checkpoint: the latter maximises over train_seed x checkpoint_round and is biased upward. Report all five training-seed distributions, every G2 threshold, and coins_share alongside score for every arm that has opponents.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reproducibility: rule_based_agent calls np.random.seed() with no argument (callbacks.py:69), so ARMS WITH OPPONENTS ARE NOT BIT-REPRODUCIBLE -- neither training nor evaluation. Every number from this arm carries that second noise source on top of training seed variance.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_loot_crate: docs/01 section 7.21: the five-seed spread of the handcrafted control gives sd 3.77, so two arms measured once each need a gap of 4.7. That threshold covers training variance; the tournament one below does not.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: docs/01 section 7.20: pooled 450-round classic-with-opponents score has sd 0.089, so two arms need a gap of 0.246 (coins_share: 0.022). This was measured by re-running ONE fixed set of checkpoints, so it is evaluation noise only and does NOT cover training variance. Use it for a paired same-seed difference, never to bless a maximum taken over seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.selection_protocol: Pool the five training seeds at each checkpoint round; pick the round on the pooled VALIDATION curve; freeze it; then read the holdout numbers at that round. Holdout is never used to decide whether to continue an arm.
